description: This record describes a dynamic hydraulic and thermal model of district heating networks built on the Lagrangian method and a discrete event simulation framework, developed in Zichan Xie's doctoral thesis at Aalto University, defended on 16 May 2025. The model uses variable time step simulation, adjusting time and space discretisation through critical sampling point identification, lazy evaluation and a tolerance threshold that removes redundant sampling points, and handles tree-shaped and meshed topologies and operating strategies such as variable flow with variable temperature. It reports delivered temperature and energy, water transmission time and heat losses; tests on a single pipe, a tree-shaped network and a meshed network of 186 pipes with 80 substations gave a mean residual standard deviation of 1.15 degrees Celsius, and an 85-day simulation ran in 0.29 seconds on a laptop. Access: the thesis PDF is free to download under Aaltodoc terms that allow personal use and prohibit commercial use; the three included articles are in Energy and Energy Conversion and Management, one still under review. Coverage is generic networks tested on real data from Finland. Caveats: no model code or licence for reuse is stated, and the meshed-network article was under review. It suits network flow and digital twin studies of district heating, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
